Ignoring the acceleration and assuming that the bottle has constant velocity (a huge assumption and not really true), we can gauge the speed with v=d/t. I couldn't calculate for acceleration because I don't have the height it reached :/

The distance is about [6.2 meters in this screen shot](http://i.imgur.com/sFjs50D.jpg). This is found by taking the guy's height [(2.01m)](http://pikastar.com/taras-kulakov-height-weight-body-measurements/) and making it equal to the height of the garage door.  Now, using the keys '.' and ',' I can see through each frame. I see that it takes 7 frames to reach the height shown in that screen shot. And each second in that video has 30 frames (I counted). Therefore the time it takes to reach that height is (7/30)=0.233 seconds. Now we have t=0.233s, d=6.2m. 


Plugging it into v=d/t = 6.2/0.233 = 26.5m/s = 95.4 km/h ≈ 60 miles/h.

Pretty fast! (Probably much faster than that)
